title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 185
text:
136 Section 9C is important not least because, in many cases,
it reverses Re Osman [1996] 1 Cr App R 126, where it was held that a person who is
profoundly deaf and unable to follow the proceedings in court, or the deliberations in the
jury room, without the assistance of an interpreter in sign language should be discharged
from jury service pursuant to s.9B because such a person could not act effectively as a juror.
That was because it was said to be an unacceptable irregularity in the proceedings for the
interpreter to retire with the jury to the jury room.

59. It should be noted that s.9C is limited in its scope to assisting people who are deaf with BSL
interpreters. That provision therefore does not deal with impairments other than deafness,
nor with people who are deaf but not assisted by BSL (eg because they use a different sign
language).
